The retrieved matches indicate that when controlling for preoperative features, the year in which RP was performed (radical prostatectomy) is indeed a predictor of outcome on multivariate analysis. This effect could not be explained by stage migration, suggesting that age itself may play a role in determining the prognosis for patients with localized prostate cancer.

In other words, researchers have found that controlling for preoperative features such as age does not fully explain the variation in outcomes between patients who underwent radical prostatectomy and those who did not. This implies that year of radical prostatectomy may be a predictor of outcome in prostate cancer, taking into account other factors such as stage.

It's essential to note that while age itself may contribute to prognosis, the specific time frame during which RP was performed (year) could potentially impact outcomes. Further research is needed to fully understand the relationship between year of radical prostatectomy and patient outcomes.
